stories.headline: Merck-Moderna personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine cuts relapse or death risk 42%; Moderna falls

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial, intismeran autogene plus Keytruda cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42% vs Keytruda alone (HR 0.58) in completely resected stage IIB-IV melanoma, after a median 24.6 months of follow-up.
key_facts.excerpt: after a median follow-up of 24.6 months, intismeran in combination with KEYTRUDA significantly reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% (HR=0.58 [95% CI, 0.45–0.75]; two-sided p<0.001)

key_facts.fact: The combination also cut the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38%; two-year recurrence-free survival was 82.2% vs 70.0% with Keytruda alone.
key_facts.excerpt: reduced the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38% (HR=0.62 ...) ... the two-year RFS rate was 82.2% ... compared to 70.0% ... for KEYTRUDA alone

key_facts.fact: After the six-month vaccine regimen, a pre-specified sensitivity analysis showed a 58% reduction in risk of recurrence or death; overall survival data are not yet mature.
key_facts.excerpt: reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 58% (piecewise HR=0.42 ...) ... Overall survival (OS) data are not yet mature

key_facts.fact: The trial enrolled 1,137 patients; the vaccine is an mRNA therapy encoding up to 34 neoantigens designed from each patient's own tumor mutations. Results go to ESMO 2026 (Presidential Symposium) and were accepted by the New England Journal of Medicine.
key_facts.excerpt: The trial enrolled 1,137 patients ... Each therapy consists of a synthetic mRNA coding for up to 34 neoantigens ... accepted for publication in The New England Journal of Medicine

key_facts.fact: Moderna shares fell as much as 25% on Thursday after partial data leaked on an oncology website, despite the results being positive relative to expectations; the stock had risen more than 530% year to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Moderna shares dropped as much as 25% on Thursday following the leak of partial data ... Moderna shares have spiked more than 530% year-to-date

key_facts.fact: Moderna closed more than 17% lower and Merck about 1.8% lower, per Reuters; the companies said they are engaging with regulators.
key_facts.excerpt: They closed more than 17% lower after the results leaked on an oncology website earlier on Thursday. Merck shares closed down about 1.8%.

stories.headline: US envoy Waltz says Iran war could last another year; Brent hits $114 as Aramco reroutes oil

key_facts.fact: US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz told the Financial Times the US is prepared for a protracted conflict with Iran and could still face a stalemate a year from now.
key_facts.excerpt: Waltz told the FT that Washington could still face a stalemate a year from now, without an agreement on Iran's nuclear programme or a return to prewar shipping levels through the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: Waltz said the US Navy can maintain its blockade of Iranian ports 'for the foreseeable future' and that US goals require Iran to dispose of its highly enriched uranium and accept a deal on domestic enrichment.
key_facts.excerpt: He added that Mr. Trump "and the U.S. Navy can maintain this blockade [on Iranian ports] for the foreseeable future" ... will not have achieved its key goals in Iran until the country disposes of its highly enriched uranium

key_facts.fact: Brent crude hit $114 a barrel on Friday after settling at $113.17 on Thursday, its highest since May.
key_facts.excerpt: The price of Brent crude oil hit $114 a barrel Friday after Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed to have disabled seven tankers near the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: Thursday's Brent settlement was $113.17, up 4.00%, its highest since May.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude ($/bbl, settle) | 113.17 | +4.00% ... Brent settled at $113.17, its highest since May

key_facts.fact: Saudi Aramco said flows through its East-West pipeline, which bypasses Hormuz, more than tripled from 2 million to 7 million barrels per day.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Aramco said Thursday that the amount of oil flowing through its East-West pipeline, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, had more than tripled from 2 million to 7 million barrels per day

key_facts.fact: Trump accused Iran on Truth Social of 'making up fake hits, mines' to drive up oil prices before the Nov. 3 midterms; a CENTCOM spokesperson said shipping lanes were cleared of mines and 95% of vessels get through.
key_facts.excerpt: "They are making up fake hits, mines, and everything else ..." ... US forces have cleared the international shipping lanes of mines ... with 95 percent of vessels getting through.

key_facts.fact: The UAE reported a tanker oil spill on Friday affecting beaches in Umm Al Quwain, which were closed.
key_facts.excerpt: Emirati authorities "detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain's beaches" ... adding that Umm Al Quwain beaches had been closed.

key_facts.fact: The war, which Trump initially expected to last four to five weeks, is approaching its ninth month.
key_facts.excerpt: The conflict, which Trump initially expected to last four to five weeks, is approaching its ninth month

stories.headline: Trump asked Musk to lift Ukraine's Starshield cap, WSJ says; Kyiv says limits persist

key_facts.fact: President Trump called Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to lift restrictions he had imposed on Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink used in Ukraine, US officials told the WSJ.
key_facts.excerpt: President Trump called Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to lift restrictions on a military-grade version of Starlink in Ukraine that the SpaceX chief had throttled, U.S. officials said.

key_facts.fact: The system was working more normally Thursday, though some Ukrainian officials said it was not restored to full functionality.
key_facts.excerpt: The system was working more normally Thursday, shortly after their conversation ... Some Ukrainian officials said the system wasn't restored to full functionality

key_facts.fact: Trump declined to confirm the call but said: 'The bottom line, he put it back.'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump refused to say whether he had called Musk ... but said: "Bottom line, he put it back."

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian defence ministry sources told the BBC drones were still losing connection at speeds of 161 km/h (100 mph), and there was no confirmation restrictions had been lifted.
key_facts.excerpt: instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded ... "currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted"

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian officials said on Friday morning the restrictions remained in place; Zelensky adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said there was no indication they had been lifted.
key_facts.excerpt: restrictions were still in place on Friday, according to Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov ... "We have not seen any indication that Starlink's restrictions have been lifted"

key_facts.fact: CNN reported Trump had sought information on the slowdown and went to Musk after Ukrainian officials reported disruptions.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump had been seeking out information about the slowdown and went to Musk after Ukrainian officials reported disruptions, the source said.

stories.headline: US Treasury proposes wider curbs on investment in Chinese AI, quantum, hypersonics and biotech

key_facts.fact: On Oct. 22 Treasury issued a proposed rule implementing the COINS Act, passed in the FY2026 defense bill, to expand its Outbound Investment Security Program.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury ... today issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to propose updates to the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) based on direction from Congress in the Comprehensive Outbound Investment Security (COINS) Act

key_facts.fact: The rule covers semiconductors, 'super intelligence' AI systems, quantum, high-performance computing, hypersonic systems and, newly added by the Secretary, biotechnology.
key_facts.excerpt: semiconductor technology and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, super intelligence systems, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and supercomputing, and biotechnology

key_facts.fact: Countries of concern are China (including Hong Kong and Macau), Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela under Maduro.
key_facts.excerpt: define a "country of concern" as the People's Republic of China (including Hong Kong and Macau), the Republic of Cuba, the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, the Russian Federation, and the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela

key_facts.fact: It would ban US investment in country-of-concern entities developing any super-intelligence system, replacing the current notification regime, and add bans on hypersonics and biotech areas such as brain-computer interfaces.
key_facts.excerpt: expands the existing prohibition to more broadly restrict U.S. person investment into country of concern entities that develop any SI system ... adds a new prohibition on ... brain computer interfaces

key_facts.fact: The rule would only apply to investments above $50,000 and exclude many financial investments, including stock purchases; Treasury will take public comments before a final rule.
key_facts.excerpt: would only apply to investments that exceed $50,000 and would exclude many financial investments, including stock purchases

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the rules would 'prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies'.
key_facts.excerpt: "The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security."

key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk has invested roughly $1 billion in Skydance ... The deal came together at roughly the same time as equity investments from Skydance's other investors, including board member Laurene Powell Jobs

key_facts.fact: Paramount closed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Oct. 6 and named the combined company Skydance, led by co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz.

key_facts.excerpt: Skydance has said it expects to see $6 billion in cost savings over three years, though it faces a debt burden of nearly $80 billion.

stories.headline: Greece passes law banning social media for children under 15 from January 2027

key_facts.fact: Greece's parliament passed a bill banning children under 15 from social media after a debate of more than 16 hours; it takes effect on Jan. 1, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Parliament approved the bill late on October 22, following a debate that lasted more than 16 hours ... restrictions set to take effect on January 1, 2027

key_facts.fact: Only the governing New Democracy party backed the bill; PASOK abstained and SYRIZA, Greek Solution, KKE, Niki and Course of Freedom voted against.
key_facts.excerpt: The New Democracy party was the only bloc in parliament to support the measure; while opposition parties SYRIZA, Greek Solution, KKE, Niki and Freedom Course voted against it, and PASOK abstained.

key_facts.fact: Platforms are responsible for age verification and face fines of up to 6% of global turnover, said Digital Governance and AI Minister Dimitris Papastergiou.
key_facts.excerpt: Η ευθύνη εφαρμογής ανήκει στις πλατφόρμες ... απειλούμενες με πρόστιμα έως και το 6% του παγκόσμιου τζίρου τους (responsibility lies with platforms ... facing fines of up to 6% of global turnover)

key_facts.fact: Parents cannot grant permission and existing accounts are not exempt; age checks can use the state Kids Wallet app, which only tells platforms whether a user is over or under 15.
key_facts.excerpt: Parents will not be able to grant permission for children to use the platforms, and existing accounts will not be exempt ... The app will tell the platform only whether the user is over or under 15

key_facts.fact: More than 20 countries have passed similar laws, per an AFP tally; Australia was first, barring under-16s.
key_facts.excerpt: Australia last year became the first country to introduce such a social media ban for kids, barring under-16s. More than 20 countries have passed similar laws, according to an AFP tally.

stories.headline: Nasdaq has worst day since June as chip index sinks 6.7%; 10-year yield falls most in 3 years

key_facts.fact: The Nasdaq fell 2.6% to 26,008.86 and the S&P 500 1.21% to 7,663.43 on Thursday, while the Dow eked out an 11.89-point gain.
key_facts.excerpt: the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 11.89 points, or 0.02%, to 52,867.98, the S&P 500 lost 93.74 points, or 1.21%, to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 694.00 points, or 2.60%, to 26,008.86

key_facts.fact: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 6.7%, its biggest daily drop since June 23, and is now more than 26% below its June 22 record close.
key_facts.excerpt: The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index ... plunged 6.7%, its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23 ... off more than 26% from its record closing high reached on June 22

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield fell below 5% for the first time in nearly a month; its nearly 0.2-point drop was the sharpest one-day fall in more than three years.
key_facts.excerpt: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield dropped below 5% for the first time in nearly a month. Its decline of nearly 0.2 percentage point was the sharpest one-day fall in more than three years.

key_facts.fact: The S&P 500 had its worst day since July, but most US stocks actually rose, as weakness was concentrated in tech.
key_facts.excerpt: The S&P 500 fell 1.2% for its worst day since July ... masked strength for the rest of the U.S. market, where the majority of stocks actually rose

key_facts.fact: Markets are pricing a probability that the Fed raises rates by another 25 basis points before year-end, with jobless claims near multi-decade lows.
key_facts.excerpt: Financial markets are currently pricing in the probability that the central bank will raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points before year-end.
